verse: Do not complain against one another, so that you may not be judged. Behold, the judge stands before the door. (Jas 5:9)
You should not complain as some of them did, and so they were destroyed by the destroyer. (1 Cor 10:10)
These are murmurers and complainers; walking according to their own lusts; and their mouth speaks proud things, admiring people for their own gain. (Jude 1:16)

Meanwhile, there arose a murmur among the people against the Lord, as if they were grief-stricken because of their labors. And when the Lord had heard it, he was angry. Then the fire of the Lord was enflamed against them, and it devoured those who were at the edge of the camp. (Num 11:1)
Be hospitable to one another without murmuring. (1 Pet 4:9)

All the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness. The Israelites said to them, ‘If only we had died by the Lord’s hand in Egypt! There we sat around pots of meat and ate bread until we were full; but you have brought us out into this desert to starve this entire assembly to death. (Exo 16:2-3)
How long will this wicked multitude grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints of these grumbling Israelites, which they complain against me. (Num 14:27)
They despised the pleasant land; they did not believe His promise. They grumbled in their tents and did not obey the Lord. (Ps 106:24-25)
According to their pasture, they were satisfied; when they were satisfied, they became proud; then they forgot Me. (Hos 13:6)
Attend to me and hear me: I mourn in my complaint and I groan. (Ps 55:2)
Why will you contend with me in judgement? you have all transgressed against me, says the Lord. (Jer 2:29)
The folly of a man leads him astray: yet his heart rages against the Lord. (Pro 19:3)
Woe to him who strives with his maker. Shall the clay say to him who fashions it: ‘What are you making?’ (Is 45:9)
But who are you, a mere human being, to talk back to God? Will what is formed say to the one who formed it, “Why did you make me like this?” (Rom 9:20)

Who can command and make it come to pass, if the Lord has not commanded it? Shall not both evil and good proceed out of the mouth of the Most High? Why should any living person complain about the punishment of his sins? (Lam 3:37-39)

One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back and with a loud voice praised God. He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet and thanked him. And he was a Samaritan. And Jesus asked, “Were not ten who were cleansed? But where are the other nine? Was no one found to return and give glory to God except this stranger?” (Luk 17:15-18)

Moses said: “In the evening, the Lord will give you flesh to eat, and in the morning, bread in fullness. For he has heard your murmurings that you have murmured against him. For what are we? Your murmuring is not against us, but against the Lord.” (Exo 16:8)

His wife said to him, “Do you still continue in your integrity? Curse God and die.” But he said to her, “You have spoken like one of the foolish wives. Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?” In all this, Job did not sin with his lips. (Job 2:9-10)

He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there; the Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” In all this Job did not sin or blame God of doing wrong. (Job 1:21-22)
To you, O God, do we give thanks, to you do we give thanks; for your name is near. We declare your wonderful things. (Ps 75:1)

Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, whose mercy endures for ever and ever. Bless the God of gods, all you who worship the Lord; praise and give thanks, for his mercy endures forever. (Dan 3:89-90)
It is a good thing to give thanks to the Lord, to sing praises to your name, O Most High; to proclaim your loving kindness in the morning, and your faithfulness by night. (Ps 92:1-2)
I will give thanks to the Lord with my whole heart, in the assembly of the upright, and in the congregation. (Ps 111:1)
Everything that God has created is good and nothing is to be rejected, if it is received with thanksgiving, for it is sanctified by the Word of God and prayer. (1 Tim 4:4-5)
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and his courts with praise. Be thankful to him and bless his name. (Ps 100:4)
I will thank you forever, for what you have done. In the presence of your faithful people, I will put my hope in your name - for it is good. (Ps 52:9)
I will give thanks to the Lord with my mouth; I will praise him among the multitude. (Ps 109:30)
Lifting up his eyes, Jesus said: “Father, I give thanks to you because you have heard me. And I know that you always hear me.” (Jn 11:41-42)
Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving and make a joyful noise unto him with songs! For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. (Ps 95:2-3)
Give thanks to the Lord and call his name. Make known his deeds among the people. Sing to him, and sing psalms to him, and tell of all His wondrous works. (1 Chron 16:8-9)
I will give thanks to you, Lord, with my whole heart. I will recount all your wonders. (Ps 9:1)
Always give thanks to God the Father for all things, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. (Eph 5:20)
Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be moved, let us be thankful, by which we serve God with fear and awe. (Heb 12:28)
I will give thanks to the Lord due for his righteousness and sing praise to the name of the Lord Most High. (Ps 7:17)
I will sacrifice unto you with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to the Lord! (Jon 2:9)
Those who offer thanksgiving as their sacrifice glorify me; to those who walk in the right way I will show the salvation of God. (Ps 50:23)
O give thanks to the Lord, call on his name, make known his deeds among the people. (Ps 105:1)
I give thanks to Christ Jesus our Lord, who has given me strength. He has considered me faithful and has appointed me to serve him. (1 Tim 1:12)
Proclaim the majesty of his name and offer thanks to him with praise, with music on the harp and with songs on your lips. (Sir 39:15)
I will praise the name of God with a song and will magnify him with thanksgiving. (Ps 69:30)
I will bless the Lord at all times; his praise shall continually be in my mouth. (Ps 34:1)
Let everything that has breath praise the Lord! (Ps 150:6)
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name. (Ps 103:1)
Thank the Lord for his loving kindness, for His wonderful works to all people. For he satisfies the thirsty and fills the hungry with good things. (Ps 107:8-9)
I will continually praise you and sing songs of thanksgiving. You heard my prayer and saved me from destruction. For this, I give thanks and praise you. (Sir 51:11)
Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth exult. And let them say among the nations, ‘The Lord reigns.’ (1 Chron 16:31)
I will tell of the Lord's loving kindness; I will praise him for all that the Lord has done for us. (Is 63:7)
Though they knew God, they did not glorify him as God or give thanks to him, but they became vain in their thoughts, and their foolish hearts were darkened. (Rom 1:21)
Make a joyful noise unto the Lord, all the earth; sing forth the glory of His name; make his praise glorious. (Ps 66:1-2)
O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth shall declare your praise. (Ps 51:15)
